extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is an environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents, containing 2,438 real-world task instances sourced from 11 Python repositories, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. In Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2025), PMLR 267. arXiv:2412.21139.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Repositories created before July 1, 2022 with >500 stars, >=300 lines of code, >500 pull requests, and >100 contributors were identified using SEART GitHub search, resulting in 358 repositories and 64,689 task instances extracted via SWE-Bench's extraction script (SWE-Gym Raw). For 11 repositories, executable environments were configured manually using requirements files, CI scripts, or documentation, and validated using unit test execution.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: GitHub issues, repository snapshots, pull requests, and test cases sourced from 11 popular open-source Python repositories (pandas, MONAI, moto, mypy, dvc, dask, modin, pydantic, conan, hydra, bokeh).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Instances were associated with version numbers using repository configuration files and scripts. Dependencies were configured per instance, and instances were verified using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure the gold patch passed more unit tests than the original code. Instances failing validation were filtered out. SWE-Gym Lite filtered instances requiring editing more than one file, poorly described problem statements, excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual configuration of dependencies for each task instance using configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or documentation from repository snapshots, followed by verification using execution-based scripts. This process required approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations were performed by a subset of the authors.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Automating software engineering tasks could enhance developer productivity, assist critical open-source infrastructure, and improve accessibility. Potential societal concerns include impacts on software engineering employment, considerations around code ownership, licensing, attribution, and the risk that techniques could be misused to automate the creation of malicious code.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern, with pandas representing nearly one-third of instances and bokeh representing 1%. Sampling agent rollouts introduces bias toward easier tasks due to the long-tail distribution of task success probability.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited environment diversity in terms of the number of repositories (11 repositories), task types, and programming languages (restricted to Python). The benchmark tasks focus solely on automated task completion rather than human-in-the-loop collaborative software engineering. Current models are research artifacts and not production-ready.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training software engineering agents via supervised fine-tuning and rejection sampling fine-tuning; training verifiers (outcome-supervised reward models) for inference-time reranking; evaluating agent scaling behaviors.
